# Preface {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
# Build a bib database for any R packages used across the book.
knitr::write_bib(
  c(.packages(), "bookdown", "knitr", "rmarkdown"),
  "packages.bib"
)
```

This book is a technical and academic treatment of marketing research. It is
written for two readers at once: the **doctoral researcher**, who wants formal
constructs, derivations, identification assumptions, and citations to the primary
literature; and the **senior technical practitioner**, who wants the intuition, the
trade-offs, and runnable code. Wherever the two pull in different directions, the
book leads with intuition and follows immediately with the formalism, so that
neither reader is short-changed.

Three commitments shape every chapter. First, **rigor**: constructs are defined
formally, methods are stated with their estimators and assumptions, and empirical
claims are tied to the primary literature in the top marketing journals. Second,
**reproducibility**: quantitative ideas are accompanied by code that runs. Third,
**verifiability**: every cited work carries a DOI, so any claim can be traced to its
source.

The book is organized into parts that move from *what* marketing studies
(constructs and substantive domains) to *how* it studies them (methodology), and
then to the advanced seminars and research craft that define the modern field. A
short history of marketing thought (see @sec-history) situates the whole
enterprise before the substantive material begins.

No formal prerequisites are required, though a reader comfortable with introductory
probability, regression, and a scripting language such as R will get the most from
the methodological chapters.

## Use this book in your AI assistant {.unnumbered}

This book is indexed by the [Research Methods Library](https://research-methods-mcp.vercel.app/), a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that makes it available to AI assistants. Given a research question, an assistant connected to the server recommends candidate study designs, states their identifying assumptions, returns runnable R and Python code, and cites the sections of this book and of the author's other works on which each answer draws. Access is free and requires no account or API key.

**Endpoint:** `https://research-methods-mcp.vercel.app/mcp`

-   **Claude** (web, desktop, and mobile): Settings → Connectors → **Add custom connector**; enter the endpoint.
-   **Claude Code:** `claude mcp add --transport http research-methods https://research-methods-mcp.vercel.app/mcp`
-   **ChatGPT:** Settings → enable developer mode → add a custom connector of type MCP server with the endpoint and no authentication.
-   **Cursor** and **Visual Studio Code:** [Add to Cursor](https://cursor.com/en/install-mcp?name=research-methods&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL3Jlc2VhcmNoLW1ldGhvZHMtbWNwLnZlcmNlbC5hcHAvbWNwIn0%3D) or [Install in VS Code](https://insiders.vscode.dev/redirect/mcp/install?name=research-methods&config=%7B%22type%22%3A%22http%22%2C%22url%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Fresearch-methods-mcp.vercel.app%2Fmcp%22%7D).

Configuration for other MCP clients is described on the [server's website](https://research-methods-mcp.vercel.app/).
:::
